name: Þingvellir rift walk: Almannagjá to Öxarárfoss
why: Down the rift between two continental plates, past the rock where Iceland's parliament met from 930, to a waterfall pouring into the crack.
book: Free walk; the park charges a parking fee at Hakið (1,000 ISK for a car). By car from Reykjavík on Route 36, or on a Golden Circle bus.
water: Toilets, water and a café at the Hakið visitor centre; nothing on the path.
dangers: Ice on the paths in winter: wear spikes or good soles.
Stay off the cliff edges and out of fenced fissures; the ground is still cracking open.
turnaround: No real turnaround: the walk is short and paved. In bad weather turn back at Lögberg.

points.name: Hakið viewpoint above Almannagjá
points.note: The platform by the visitor centre on the rim of the North American plate: the whole rift valley and Þingvallavatn below. The path drops into the gorge from here.

points.name: Lögberg, the Law Rock
points.note: Where the laws were recited at the Alþingi from 930 to 1262; a flagpole marks it. The path then passes Drekkingarhylur pool.

points.name: Öxarárfoss
points.note: A fall of almost 13 m into Stekkjargjá; the river was probably diverted into the rift in the Middle Ages. Back the same way, or by the river past the church.
